summary: Tested session isolation on user switch for River Watch AIS app. The core session isolation logic is WORKING CORRECTLY when logout is performed via the API. However, there is a UX issue: the SetupPage is missing a logout button, making it impossible for users to logout from that page through the UI.

ui_bugs.issue: Missing logout button - users cannot logout from SetupPage through UI
ui_bugs.details: SetupPage only has 'Change' button which clears localStorage but doesn't call logout API. Users stuck on SetupPage cannot switch accounts.

passed_tests: Session isolation works correctly when logout API is called
User1 MMSI (USER1_MMSI_111) correctly stored after login
User2 MMSI (USER2_MMSI_222) correctly stored after login
User2 sees only their own vessel data after User1 logout
User1's MMSI not found in User2's session
User1's boat name not found in User2's session
AuthContext.jsx logout function correctly clears localStorage
App.js useEffect correctly clears session data when user is null
Backend /api/auth/logout endpoint returns 200 and clears session
failed_tests: Cannot logout from SetupPage via UI - no logout button available
action_items: Add logout button to SetupPage - users need ability to switch accounts from this page
Consider adding a header component with user menu that appears on all authenticated pages
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.jsx logout function (line 115-130) correctly clears localStorage
App.js useEffect (line 165-190) correctly clears session data when user logs out
SetupPage.jsx handleClearSession (line 110-118) only clears localStorage, doesn't call logout API - this is the root cause of the UX issue
SetupPage reads MMSI from localStorage (line 30) which gets re-populated by App.js from user account data

success_rate.frontend: 90% (session isolation works, but SetupPage missing logout button)

seed_data_creation: Test users already existed with vessels configured
context_for_next_testing_agent: Session isolation is working correctly when logout API is called. The issue is that SetupPage doesn't have a logout button, so users on that page cannot switch accounts through the UI. The 'Change' button on SetupPage only clears localStorage but doesn't call the logout API, and App.js re-populates localStorage from user account data. Fix: Add logout button to SetupPage that calls the logout function from AuthContext.

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: SetupPage is missing a logout button. The 'Change' button only clears localStorage but doesn't call the logout API. Since App.js re-populates localStorage from the user's account data on mount, clearing localStorage alone doesn't prevent session bleed.
reproduction_steps: 2. User lands on SetupPage (no connectionConfig set)
3. Try to logout - no logout button available
5. Navigate to login page - user is still authenticated
6. App.js re-populates localStorage from User1's account
7. Login as User2 - User1's MMSI still shows in SetupPage
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Add logout button to SetupPage that calls useAuth().logout() function. This will properly clear the session cookie and localStorage.
